main_point.en: Jesus meets our needs to help us see Him and know Him.
main_point.zh-Hant: 耶穌滿足我們的需要，幫助我們看見祂並認識祂。

christ_connection.en: From the beginning of Jesus’s earthly ministry, the people recognized that He was different. Jesus performed miracles to fulfill the purpose of His earthly ministry and to show that He is the Son of God, the One who came to proclaim and provide salvation.
christ_connection.zh-Hant: 從耶穌在地上的事工一開始，人們就認出祂與眾不同。耶穌行神蹟，是要成就祂在地上事工的目的，並顯明祂是神的兒子，就是那位前來宣告並帶來救恩的主。

title.zh-Hant: 耶穌賜下更美好的事物

content.en:
1 On the third day there was a wedding at Cana in Galilee, and the mother of Jesus was there. 
2 Jesus also was invited to the wedding with his disciples. 
3 When the wine ran out, the mother of Jesus said to him, “They have no wine.” 
4 And Jesus said to her, “Woman, what does this have to do with me? My hour has not yet come.” 
5 His mother said to the servants, “Do whatever he tells you.” 
6 Now there were six stone water jars there for the Jewish rites of purification, each holding twenty or thirty gallons. 
7 Jesus said to the servants, “Fill the jars with water.” And they filled them up to the brim. 
8 And he said to them, “Now draw some out and take it to the master of the feast.” So they took it.
content.zh-Hant:
1 第三日，在加利利的迦拿有娶親的筵席，耶穌的母親在那裏。
2 耶穌和他的門徒也被請去赴席。
3 酒用盡了，耶穌的母親對他說：「他們沒有酒了。」
4 耶穌說：「母親，我與你有甚麼相干？我的時候還沒有到。」
5 他母親對用人說：「他告訴你們甚麼，你們就做甚麼。」
6 照猶太人潔淨的規矩，有六口石缸擺在那裏，每口可以盛兩三桶水。
7 耶穌對用人說：「把缸倒滿了水。」他們就倒滿了，直到缸口。
8 耶穌又說：「現在可以舀出來，送給管筵席的。」他們就送了去。

title.zh-Hant: 耶穌的神蹟顯明祂的身分

content.en:
9 When the master of the feast tasted the water now become wine, and did not know where it came from (though the servants who had drawn the water knew), the master of the feast called the bridegroom 
10 and said to him, “Everyone serves the good wine first, and when people have drunk freely, then the poor wine. But you have kept the good wine until now.” 
11 This, the first of his signs, Jesus did at Cana in Galilee, and manifested his glory. And his disciples believed in him.
content.zh-Hant:
9 管筵席的嘗了那水變的酒，並不知道是哪裏來的，只有舀水的用人知道。管筵席的便叫新郎來，
10 對他說：「人都是先擺上好酒，等客喝足了，才擺上次的，你倒把好酒留到如今！」
11 這是耶穌所行的頭一件神蹟，是在加利利的迦拿行的，顯出他的榮耀來；他的門徒就信他了。

content.en: Leaders: Jesus’s words and actions pointed to His identity (2:11). May our words and actions reveal His identity as the Savior—the One who redeemed us and made us new.
content.zh-Hant: 帶領者：耶穌的言語和行動指向祂的身分（2:11）。願我們的言語和行動顯明祂就是救主——那位救贖我們、使我們成為新造之人的主。

title.zh-Hant: 耶穌賜下更美好的事物

content.en: “Running out of wine represented a social disaster much greater in the first century than it would today. Disgrace, humiliation, insult—all these and more would be brought upon the family with such carelessness as to allow this to happen. Wedding celebrations in that day sometimes lasted nearly a week, so the wine supply was a major consideration.”¹
content.zh-Hant: 「在第一世紀，酒用盡所代表的社會災難，遠比今天嚴重。這樣的疏忽會使全家蒙受羞辱、屈辱、侮辱——以及更多難堪的後果。當時的婚宴有時會持續將近一週，因此酒的供應是需要慎重考量的大事。」1

content.en: “If you or I called our mother ‘woman,’ it would be disrespectful, but in that culture this title was not mean, rude, or disrespectful. In fact, it’s the same way Jesus addresses Mary when he’s dying on the cross: ‘When Jesus saw his mother and the disciple he loved standing there, he said to his mother, “Woman, here is your son”’ (John 19:26).”²
content.zh-Hant: 「如果你我稱呼自己的母親為『女人』，那會是不尊重；但在那個文化中，這個稱呼並不意味著刻薄、粗魯或不尊重。事實上，耶穌在十字架上臨死時，就是以同樣的方式稱呼馬利亞：『耶穌見母親和他所愛的那門徒站在旁邊，就對他母親說：「母親，看，你的兒子！」』（約翰福音 19:26）。」2

content.en: “The inclusion of this detail shows us that the rituals associated with the old covenant are giving way to something far greater. The shadow found in the law has been replaced by the substance. Now that Jesus is here, things have changed. The water of ceremony has been replaced with something far better. External purification has given way to internal cleansing.”³
content.zh-Hant: 「這個細節的記載向我們顯明，與舊約有關的儀式正讓位給遠為偉大的事物。律法中的影兒已被實體取代。如今耶穌已經來了，事情改變了。禮儀用的水已被遠為美好的事物取代。外在的潔淨已讓位給內在的潔淨。」3

title.zh-Hant: 耶穌的神蹟顯明祂的身分

content.en: “The master of ceremonies’ exclamation of surprise at the quality of this ‘new wine’ compared to that served earlier (v. 10) takes us to the heart of the ‘sign’ and its meaning. The ‘new wine’ of the kingdom brought by Jesus contrasts with the old wine of Judaism. ‘Jesus changes the water of Judaism into the wine of Christianity.’ . . . This miracle can happen again as the water of guilt, habitual failure and legalism, is transformed by the word of the risen Jesus into the wine of forgiveness, victory and joyful obedience.”⁴
content.zh-Hant: 「管筵席的人對這『新酒』的品質感到驚訝，因為它比先前供應的酒好（第10節）；這帶我們觸及『神蹟』及其意義的核心。耶穌帶來的國度之『新酒』，與猶太教的舊酒形成對比。『耶穌把猶太教的水變成基督教的酒。』……這個神蹟也能再次發生：罪疚、一再失敗和律法主義的水，藉著復活的耶穌的話語，被轉變成赦免、得勝和喜樂的順服之酒。」4

content.en: Today’s passage is full of Jewish cultural implications that are sometimes difficult for modern readers to understand. Ancient Jewish weddings were significant moments in a community, and the celebration lasted up to an entire week. Families were expected to provide for guests; running out of food, drinks, and so on brought shame on the family, and in some cases, lawsuits for not honoring the traditional agreement! Mary asking Jesus to help reflected these cultural expectations. Modern readers are also alarmed at Jesus calling Mary “woman,” but the term wasn’t disrespectful. Jesus used this same term during the crucifixion when He asked John to care for her as his own mother (John 19:26). Many scholars believe Jesus’s conversation with Mary revealed His commitment to do the Father’s will first, even when what He willed was in opposition to opinions of Jesus’s loved ones. Rather than immediately agreeing to perform a miracle, Jesus confirmed the time was appropriate with His Father. Though the hour for Jesus’s death hadn’t come, the time for His public ministry had, and His first miracle pointed to His final hour.
content.zh-Hant: 今天的經文段落充滿猶太文化的含義，現代讀者有時很難理解。古代猶太人的婚禮是社群中的重要時刻，慶祝活動最長可持續整整一週。家庭被期待要供應賓客；食物、飲料等用盡會使家族蒙羞，在某些情況下，還會因未遵守傳統約定而遭到訴訟！馬利亞請耶穌幫忙，反映出這些文化期待。現代讀者也會對耶穌稱馬利亞為「女人」感到驚訝，但這個稱呼並不不尊重。耶穌在被釘十字架時，請約翰像照顧自己的母親一樣照顧她（約翰福音 19:26），也使用了同樣的稱呼。許多學者相信，耶穌與馬利亞的對話顯明祂委身於先遵行父的旨意，即使祂所定意的事與祂所愛之人的看法相反。耶穌沒有立即同意行神蹟，而是向父確認時機是否合宜。雖然耶穌受死的時候還沒有到，祂公開事奉的時候已經到了，而祂所行的第一個神蹟指向祂最後的時刻。

content.en: A miracle is an event in which God makes an exception to the natural order of things, or defies natural laws, for the purpose of demonstrating His glory and/or validating His message. Miracles are recorded throughout Scripture; miraculous signs and wonders were often evident when a prophet or an apostle was speaking God’s message to the people. Because we believe God to be all-powerful and personally involved in this world, we believe He can and does perform miracles.
content.zh-Hant: 神蹟是神為了彰顯祂的榮耀和／或證實祂的信息，而使自然秩序出現例外，或超越自然律的一件事。聖經各處都記載了神蹟；當先知或使徒向百姓傳講神的信息時，往往有明顯的神蹟奇事相伴。因為我們相信神是全能的，並且親自介入這個世界，所以我們相信祂能夠行神蹟，也確實會行神蹟。

content.en: God, thank you for revealing your son to us. Thank you for the signs which proved Jesus’s identity. They are evidence of your kindness— your understanding that we are often prone to unbelief. We trust in your word, and we believe in your son.
content.zh-Hant: 神啊，感謝祢向我們顯明祢的兒子。感謝祢所賜的神蹟，證明耶穌的身分。這些都是祢恩慈的證據，也顯明祢知道我們常常容易不信。我們信靠祢的話，也相信祢的兒子。

question.en: Let’s check in on how you’re doing spiritually. Last week, we talked about telling others about Jesus— about the hope we have in the gospel. Did you have opportunities to share the gospel last week? Did you share it? If not, why?
question.zh-Hant: 讓我們檢視一下自己目前的屬靈狀況。上週我們談到向他人傳講耶穌——談到我們在福音裡所擁有的盼望。上週你有機會分享福音嗎？你有分享嗎？如果沒有，為什麼？

instructions.en:
These optional activities are designed to help your students interact. You’ll find a Discussion Activity and a Cultural Connection, which touches on a relevant topic in today’s teen culture. Each group is different, so adapt these activities to fit your group’s needs. The goal is for students to connect more to the lesson as they connect to the topic and to one another.

Ask the following questions, allowing time for students to share responses:
instructions.zh-Hant:
這些可選的活動是為了幫助你的學生互動而設計的。你會看到一個討論活動和一個文化連結，後者觸及今日青少年文化中一個相關的議題。每個小組都不一樣，所以要調整這些活動，以配合你小組的需要。目標是讓學生在與主題和彼此建立連結的同時，更深入地投入這一課。

提出以下問題，給學生時間分享回應：

question.en: Have you ever held off on a good opportunity because you knew a better offer was coming? What was that like?
question.zh-Hant: 你是否曾經因為知道更好的提議即將出現，而暫緩接受一個很好的機會？那是什麼感受？

question.en: When have you taken a lesser offer and been disappointed that you didn’t wait for something better?
question.zh-Hant: 你何時曾接受一個較差的提議，後來因為沒有等待更好的事物而感到失望？

question.en: Why is it difficult to wait for something better instead of settling for what’s good in the moment?
question.zh-Hant: 為什麼等待更好的事物，而不是滿足於當下的美好事物，會很困難？

content.en: Holding out for a better offer is sometimes difficult. We’re tempted to settle for something good instead of waiting for the very best. In today’s lesson, Jesus will provide something good for His friends, but the miracle only pointed to something better—His sacrifice for our sin.
content.zh-Hant: 等待更好的提議有時很困難。我們受到誘惑，寧可滿足於某件美好的事物，也不等候那最好的事物。在今天的課程中，耶穌會為祂的朋友提供某件美好的事物，但這神蹟只是指向更美好的事物——祂為我們的罪所作的犧牲。

cultural_connection.en: Have you ever promised to do better—to be a better person, friend, son, or daughter? Or maybe you wanted to be a better athlete or student, a better brother or sister. Our efforts to be better often fall short. We try for a while, but we revert back to old patterns and behaviors. The truth is that we can’t be better on our own. When it comes to sin, we can’t do better at all. Our efforts to be good will come up short. The more we try to be good enough apart from Jesus, the more disappointed and ashamed we’ll feel. The good news is that Jesus doesn’t just help us be better; Jesus makes us new (2 Cor. 5:17). He changes us into something we’re not. This transformation is a beautiful exchange that none of us deserve; we receive Jesus’s righteousness in exchange for Him taking our sin. So, can you be a better person, friend, daughter, son? No, Jesus makes you even better than better; He makes you new.
cultural_connection.zh-Hant: 你是否曾承諾要做得更好——成為更好的人、更好的朋友、更好的兒子或女兒？也許你想成為更好的運動員或學生，或更好的兄弟姊妹。我們想變得更好的努力常常達不到目標。我們努力一段時間，卻又回到舊有的模式和行為。事實是，靠自己無法變得更好。面對罪，我們根本無法做得更好。我們行善的努力終究會落空。我們越想撇開耶穌、靠自己做到足夠好，就越會感到失望和羞愧。好消息是，耶穌不只是幫助我們變得更好；耶穌使我們成為新造的人（哥林多後書 5:17）。祂把我們改變成與原來不同的樣子。這個轉變是一場我們都不配得的美好交換；我們領受耶穌的義，以祂承擔我們的罪作為交換。所以，你能成為更好的人、更好的朋友、更好的女兒或兒子嗎？不能，耶穌使你不只是變得更好；祂使你成為新造的人。

title.zh-Hant: 耶穌賜下更美好的事物

question.en: Would people today expect Jesus to be invited to a fun event? What does Jesus being invited show us?
question.zh-Hant: 今天的人會期待耶穌受邀參加一個歡樂的活動嗎？耶穌受邀顯明了什麼？

answer.en: We often have a skewed view of Jesus— m­aybe because of how shows and movies depict Him or because we don’t have a deep understanding of Jewish culture. Jesus is often portrayed as always serious, always pointing out sin, never having fun. But Jesus was fully human, and based on passages like this and others where crowds and children flocked to Him, we get a better glimpse of who He was: Jesus radiated love and joy. People were drawn to Him. Jesus didn’t separate Himself from people; He had friends! He celebrated their joyful occasions and spent time with them.
answer.zh-Hant: 我們常常對耶穌抱持扭曲的看法——也許是因為影集和電影對祂的描繪方式，或者因為我們不深入了解猶太文化。耶穌常被描繪成總是嚴肅、總是在指出罪、從不享受樂趣的形象。但耶穌完全是人，而根據像這段經文，以及其他記載群眾和孩童蜂擁到祂面前的經文，我們得以更清楚地看見祂是誰：耶穌散發出愛與喜樂。 人們被祂吸引。耶穌沒有把自己與人群隔開；祂有朋友！祂慶祝他們喜樂的場合，也花時間與他們相處。

question.en: What did Mary’s instructions reveal about her view of Jesus (v. 5)? What role did the servers’ obedience play in the miracle?
question.zh-Hant: 馬利亞的吩咐顯明她如何看待耶穌（第5節）？僕人的順服在神蹟中扮演了什麼角色？

answer.en: Jesus didn’t answer Mary directly, but she trusted the outcome to Him. After bringing the problem to her son, Mary felt the freedom to walk away. What if we trusted Jesus so much that we rested in His ability to handle every part of our lives? The servers did what Jesus asked and simply filled the jars. Their small act of obedience opened the door for miraculous transformation and played a huge role in Jesus’s first miracle. Like Mary, we can trust Jesus; like the servers, our obedience matters more than we know.
answer.zh-Hant: 耶穌沒有直接回答馬利亞，但她把結果交託給祂。把問題帶到兒子面前後，馬利亞就可以放心離開了。如果我們如此信靠耶穌，以致安息於祂有能力處理我們生命中的每一個部分，會怎樣呢？ 僕人照耶穌的吩咐去做，只是把缸裝滿。他們這個小小的順服行動，為神蹟般的改變敞開了大門，並在耶穌所行的第一個神蹟中發揮了巨大的作用。我們可以像馬利亞一樣信靠耶穌；像僕人一樣，我們的順服比自己所知道的更重要。

question.en: What was the jars’ purpose (v. 6)? How does knowing their purpose help us understand the meaning of the miracle?
question.zh-Hant: 水缸的用途是什麼（第6節）？知道它們的用途如何幫助我們理解這個神蹟的意義？

answer.en: The six jars of water were in place for guests to cleanse themselves before eating, not for drinking. The jars were part of the Jews’ purity rituals. Jesus changed their purpose, though. Let’s zero in on the depth of this first miracle and the radical statement it conveyed. Jews ritually and physically cleansed themselves with water. But water could never cleanse them, or us, internally. Jesus’s blood washes us clean from our sin. He purifies us internally, which is then reflected externally by how we live—in our actions, our words, our thoughts. Jesus’s first miracle pointed to a greater miracle: The temporary cleansing that the law and the sacrificial system provided would be fulfilled in Him! Jesus’s sacrifice ushered in a way to be cleansed permanently by calling on Him for salvation. This miracle was a sign that the new covenant was coming—the one God promised would change us from the inside out (Jer. 31:33-34) and the one that would provide “rivers of living water” deep within us through the Holy Spirit (John 7:38). The water in these jars pointed to the great salvation that was on the way!
answer.zh-Hant: 這六口水缸是讓賓客在吃飯前潔淨自己用的，不是用來飲用的。這些缸是猶太人潔淨儀式的一部分。然而，耶穌改變了它們的用途。讓我們聚焦於這第一個神蹟的深度，以及它所傳達的徹底宣告。猶太人用水在禮儀上和身體上潔淨自己。但水永遠無法在內裡潔淨他們，也無法潔淨我們。耶穌的血洗淨我們的罪。祂在內裡潔淨我們，然後這種潔淨會藉著我們的生活方式——我們的行動、言語和思想——在外在反映出來。耶穌的第一個神蹟指向一個更大的神蹟：律法和獻祭制度所提供的暫時潔淨，要在祂裡面得著成全！耶穌的犧牲開啟了一條藉著呼求祂而得著永久潔淨的道路。 這個神蹟是一個兆頭，表明新約即將來臨——這約是神所應許的，要從內到外改變我們（耶利米書 31:33-34），也要藉著聖靈在我們裡面深處賜下「活水的江河」（約翰福音 7:38）。這些缸裡的水指向即將來臨的偉大救恩！

title.zh-Hant: 耶穌的神蹟顯明祂的身分

question.en: How does this miracle help you see that Jesus cares about more than just our needs? How have you seen Him work in small ways in your life?
question.zh-Hant: 這個神蹟如何幫助你看見耶穌關心的不只是我們的需要？你在自己的生活中曾看見祂以哪些微小的方式工作？

answer.en: This wedding party probably seems insignificant to most of us. The party ended, and everyone went home. Was the need for more wine really that big of a deal? Well, outside of the Jews’ cultural expectations that meant the family would be looked down on (and maybe even treated as outcasts or sued) for not providing for guests, no. They could’ve survived without it, but Jesus revealed His identity through meeting a desire. He cares deeply about us, a care extending beyond our needs only. Jesus works in seemingly insignificant moments in our lives too. When we have spiritual eyes to notice His work, then we gain a deeper understanding of His love and His character.
answer.zh-Hant: 這個婚宴對我們大多數人來說，很可能顯得微不足道。宴會結束後，大家都回家了。再多一點酒的需要真的有那麼嚴重嗎？嗯，若不考慮猶太人的文化期待，答案是否定的；按照這些期待，那個家庭若沒有供應賓客，就會被人看不起（甚至可能被視為受排斥的人或遭到起訴）。他們沒有酒也能撐過去，但耶穌藉著滿足一個願望顯明了祂的身分。祂深深地關心我們，祂的關心不只限於我們的需要。耶穌也在我們生命中看似微不足道的時刻工作。 當我們有屬靈的眼光察覺祂的工作時，就會更深地明白祂的愛和祂的品格。

question.en: Why did Jesus perform miracles? Do we still trust God to do miracles today? Have you seen any?
question.zh-Hant: 耶穌為什麼行神蹟？我們今天仍然相信神會行神蹟嗎？你曾看過神蹟嗎？

answer.en: This miracle was the first of many Jesus performed, but every miracle served the similar purpose of revealing Jesus’s identity. At the wedding in Cana, Jesus didn’t just supply a little more wine to get the family through the party. He had the servers fill the jars to the brim. They overflowed with new wine—with the very best wine. Jesus transformed water into something else entirely. The miracle pointed to something greater: Jesus gave abundantly of Himself, of His blood, for us. His sacrifice was so pure, so perfect, that it was enough to cover all sin for all time, like a fountain that never stops and is overflowing (Zech. 13:1). Miracles still happen; God still heals and restores. As believers, we are evidence of His transforming power.
answer.zh-Hant: 這個神蹟是耶穌所行的許多神蹟中的第一個，但每一個神蹟都具有大致相同的目的，就是顯明耶穌的身分。在迦拿的婚宴上，耶穌不只是供應多一點酒，讓這家人撐過宴會。祂讓僕人把缸裝滿，直到缸口。缸裡滿溢著新酒——最好的酒。耶穌把水完全變成了另一種東西。這個神蹟指向更偉大的事：耶穌豐豐富富地把自己和祂的血賜給我們。祂的犧牲如此純潔、如此完美，足以遮蓋歷代所有的罪，就像永不止息、滿溢的泉源（撒迦利亞書 13:1）。 神蹟仍然會發生；神仍然醫治並恢復人。作為信徒，我們就是祂改變的大能的證據。

question.en: How did the miracle affect Jesus’s new followers?
question.zh-Hant: 這個神蹟對耶穌新近的跟隨者有何影響？

answer.en: After witnessing the miracle, Jesus’s new disciples believed in Him (v. 11). The Jews knew God’s promise to send another prophet like Moses (Deut. 18:15). Maybe the miracle mirrored the first plague, when God, through Moses, changed the Nile River to blood as judgment on Egypt (Ex. 7:19). Jesus, the greater Moses, changed water to wine—a symbol of joy and abundance. Jesus provided wine at a literal wedding, but He also provided everything we need for another wedding—one to which He and Scripture both point (Rev. 19:7-8). The Bible refers to the church as the Bride and Christ as the Bridegroom. We are clothed in white, cleansed and prepared for this great wedding instead of the judgment we deserve.
answer.zh-Hant: 目睹這神蹟後，耶穌新近的門徒就信了祂（第11節）。猶太人知道神應許要差遣另一位像摩西一樣的先知（申命記 18:15）。也許這個神蹟讓人想起第一場災，當時神藉著摩西把尼羅河變成血，作為對埃及的審判（出埃及記 7:19）。耶穌是更大的摩西，祂把水變成酒——這是喜樂和豐盛的象徵。 耶穌在一場實際的婚宴上提供酒，但祂也供應我們參加另一場婚宴所需的一切——耶穌和聖經都指向這場婚宴（啟示錄 19:7-8）。聖經稱教會為新婦，稱基督為新郎。我們穿上白衣，被潔淨並預備好參加這場偉大的婚宴，而不是面對我們應得的審判。

question.en: God can change water into something else entirely, so why do we struggle to trust him with big and small details of our lives?
question.zh-Hant: 神能把水完全變成另一樣東西，那麼，為甚麼我們仍難以在生命中大大小小的事上信靠祂？

answer.en: When we read about Jesus’s miracles and the great wonders God did in the Old Testament, we often separate them from our own lives. We believe these accounts are true; we just doubt that God can or will work like this for us. When Jesus changed water to wine, He didn’t just add something to the water; He transformed it entirely and made it something it wasn’t before. God does the same thing with your heart, changing it from stone to flesh and helping you to follow Him (Ezek. 11:19). He gives you the Holy Spirit, empowering you to live for Him in a way you can’t do on your own. This truth is a miracle. Every single day God works a miracle in your heart by living within you! Every breath you inhale and exhale is a miracle. We sometimes forget that the God of all creation shares His Spirit with us. God works all around you and within you. He uses the big stuff in your life, of course. But He uses the small stuff too. God has only ever been faithful. You can trust God, who has transformed you, with every part of your life—big and small.
answer.zh-Hant: 當我們讀到耶穌的神蹟和神在舊約中所行的大奇事時，我們常常把它們與自己的生活分開。我們相信這些記載是真的；只是懷疑神是否能夠或是否願意為我們做同樣的事。耶穌把水變成酒時，祂不只是往水裡加了某種東西；祂完全改變了水，使它成為原本不是的樣子。神也同樣對待你的心，把石心變成肉心，幫助你跟隨祂（以西結書 11:19）。祂賜給你聖靈，使你得著能力，以靠自己無法做到的方式為祂而活。這個真理 就是 一個神蹟。神住在你裡面，每一天都在你的心中行一個神蹟！你吸入和呼出的每一口氣都是一個神蹟。我們有時忘記，創造萬物的神與我們分享祂的靈。神在你周圍和你裡面工作。祂當然使用你生命中的大事，但祂也使用小事。神一直都是信實的。你可以在生命的每一部分——無論大小——都信靠那位已經改變你的神。

content.en:
When we read through the miracles of Jesus in the Gospels, we see Jesus meet two kinds of needs: physical and spiritual. Miracles show us that only Jesus can meet both. This is a big deal because being physical and spiritual is what makes us human. God knows this because He made us, so only He can care for us completely. He cares about our eternal life, but He also cares about the here and now.

We don’t just see this truth in the Gospels but also in the Old Testament. Look again at verses 14-19 and pay attention to how David described God’s love and care for us. The actions that God takes toward us are unbelievable! Each word in these verses is filled with so much intention and purpose. God helps us, sees us, feeds us, and satisfies us. He is a good and giving God!

God is always reaching toward us. Are we receiving His love and walking in it? The way God works in our lives can be a mystery. On our worst days, we may take our frustration out on God; we may accuse Him of not meeting our needs. But God never leaves us, and His care for us is constant. Other people and situations in life will let us down, but God always remains the same, regardless of how bad life gets. He sees the big picture and is working a greater, eternal plan. God’s goodness and faithfulness should lead us to praise Him and speak about Him to others, just as David did.
content.zh-Hant:
當我們讀四福音書中耶穌所行的神蹟時，會看見耶穌滿足兩類需要：身體的和屬靈的。神蹟向我們顯明，只有耶穌能同時滿足這兩方面。這一點十分重要，因為我們之所以為人，正是因為我們既有身體，也有靈性。神知道這一點，因為祂創造了我們；所以，只有祂能全然照顧我們。祂關心我們的永生，也關心此時此地的需要。

我們不只在四福音書中看見這個真理，也在舊約中看見。請再看看第14-19節，留意大衛如何描述神對我們的愛與看顧。神為我們所做的，實在令人驚嘆！這幾節中的每一個字，都滿載著心意與目的。神幫助我們、看見我們、餵養我們，並使我們滿足。祂是一位良善、慷慨賜予人的神！

神總是向我們伸出手。我們是否正領受祂的愛，並行在其中？神在我們生命中工作的方式，可能是個奧祕。在我們最糟糕的日子裡，我們可能會把挫折發洩在神身上；我們也可能指責祂沒有滿足我們的需要。但神永不離開我們，祂對我們的看顧恆久不變。人生中的其他人和境遇會令我們失望，但無論人生變得多麼糟糕，神始終不改變。祂看見全貌，並正在成就一個更宏大、關乎永恆的計畫。神的良善與信實，應當引導我們讚美祂，並像大衛一樣向別人述說祂。

question.en: How have you seen God meet both physical and spiritual needs in your life? Why is it important to remember that God cares about both types of needs?
question.zh-Hant: 你曾如何看見神在你生命中同時滿足身體和屬靈的需要？為甚麼記得神關心這兩類需要很重要？

question.en: What needs (both big and small) do you have in your life right now that you haven’t brought to God?
question.zh-Hant: 你目前生命中有哪些需要，無論大小，是你還沒有帶到神面前的？

prayer.en: Lord, thank you for caring about every part of me. Nothing is hidden from you, and you know what’s best for me. Help me to trust you and to come to you for all of my needs.
prayer.zh-Hant: 主啊，感謝祢關心我的每一部分。我沒有任何事能向祢隱藏，祢也知道甚麼對我最好。求祢幫助我信靠祢，讓我帶著一切需要來到祢面前。

content.en:
One of the most beautiful things about being a Christian is that you can rest when the world can’t. When you catch up on the latest news, you probably aren’t encouraged. For the most part, the news showcases the bad things that are happening around the world. There may be the occasional update that is positive, but for the most part, the news shows a picture of unrest.

Yesterday’s passage reminded us that God truly cares for us, even when life may not make sense in the moment. One way that God cares for His children is by giving us what we need when complete chaos is raging around us. Let’s put ourselves in the shoes of the prophet Elijah for a minute. God used Elijah to speak God’s truth to His people who were worshiping the false god Baal. God’s own people, the nation of Israel, strayed away from Him and gave into the chaos of false worship. They followed cultural norms instead of God’s truth. God gave Elijah a message to deliver to Israel’s king: A drought and famine would come to Israel because of their disobedience.

Even though Elijah was outnumbered, God took care of him because Elijah was faithful. Even though Israel would be hungry and thirsty, Elijah wouldn’t be. The way God took care of Elijah is incredible! So, when those around you seem to be caving into chaos, you have the option to rest because God cares for you and always works for your good. Keep your eyes on God and know He will never leave you.
content.zh-Hant:
作基督徒最美好的事情之一，就是當世界無法安歇時，你卻可以安息。當你查看最新新聞時，大概不會受到鼓舞。大多數時候，新聞呈現的都是世界各地正在發生的壞事。偶爾或許也會有正面的報導，但整體來說，新聞展現的是一幅動盪不安的景象。

昨天的經文提醒我們，即使當下的人生看來令人費解，神仍真切地看顧我們。神看顧祂兒女的其中一種方式，就是在四周一片混亂時，仍供應我們所需。讓我們暫且設身處地，想像自己是先知以利亞。神使用以利亞，向那些敬拜假神巴力的百姓傳講神的真理。神自己的百姓以色列人偏離了祂，陷入錯謬敬拜的混亂中。他們跟隨文化習俗，而不是神的真理。神賜給以利亞一個信息，要他傳給以色列王：以色列會因悖逆而遭遇乾旱與饑荒。

儘管以利亞勢單力薄，神仍看顧他，因為以利亞忠心。即使以色列人要忍受飢餓乾渴，以利亞卻不必如此。神看顧以利亞的方式實在奇妙！因此，當你周圍的人似乎紛紛向混亂屈服時，你可以選擇安息，因為神看顧你，並且總是為你的益處動工。定睛於神，並知道祂永不離開你。

question.en: In your life, what kind of distractions and chaos are you tempted to give in to instead of resting in God’s care?
question.zh-Hant: 在你的生命中，有哪些使你分心的事和混亂，會誘惑你向它們屈服，而不安息在神的看顧中？

question.en: What would it look like for you to resist those temptations and rest in God’s presence?
question.zh-Hant: 對你來說，抗拒這些誘惑並安息在神的同在中，會是甚麼樣子？

prayer.en: Lord, I confess that at times I’m tempted to do things that don’t please you. Help me to remember that you are better and that you will never let me down.
prayer.zh-Hant: 主啊，我承認有時我會受誘惑，去做祢不喜悅的事。求祢幫助我記得，祢遠勝一切，並且祢永不使我失望。

content.en:
Wants and needs are completely different. You may want those new shoes to show off to your friends, but you definitely don’t need them. Wanting nice shoes or the newest phone isn’t bad, but when we obsess over new things and think we need them, we are heading the wrong way!

God knows exactly what we need and when we need it. He knows what we can handle in each season of our lives. Although we should bring every desire that we have to God, we should also trust Him with the results. Can you imagine what this world would be like if every single person got what they wanted every time they asked? Talk about a disaster waiting to happen! Thankfully, God helps us with this.

Yesterday we read from 1 Kings 17:1-7 about Israel experiencing a drought and famine because of their worship of the false god, Baal. The one person who was spared from all of this was Elijah. God then continued to provide for Elijah. As he journeyed, a widow gave him some bread and water. It was just what he needed for the next step along the way. God would make sure Elijah’s needs were being met, but he would do so in a way that required Elijah to remain completely dependent on Him for every bite of food and drink of water. Elijah would experience God’s hand in each step of the journey.

Sometimes God provides for us in huge ways, where a breakthrough seems to happen and everything changes. Other times, He gives us just what we need in a moment, so that we can learn contentment and remember to trust Him. How will you trust Him in either situation?
content.zh-Hant:
想要與需要截然不同。你可能想要那雙新鞋，好在朋友面前炫耀，但你肯定不需要它。想要漂亮的鞋子或最新的手機並不是壞事，但當我們一心迷戀新東西，還以為自己非要不可時，我們就走錯方向了！

神清楚知道我們需要甚麼，也知道我們何時需要。祂知道在人生每個季節，我們能承受甚麼。雖然我們應當把每一個願望都帶到神面前，卻也應當把結果交託給祂。你能想像，如果世上每一個人每次一開口，就得到自己想要的一切，這個世界會變成甚麼樣子嗎？那可真是一場蓄勢待發的災難！幸好，神會在這方面幫助我們。

昨天，我們讀了列王紀上 17:1-7，談到以色列因敬拜假神巴力而遭遇乾旱與饑荒。唯一免受這一切苦難的人，就是以利亞。後來，神繼續供應以利亞。在他的旅途中，一位寡婦給了他一些餅和水，正好是他下一段路程所需的。神必定會讓以利亞的需要得到滿足，卻會用一種方式來供應，使以利亞每吃一口食物、每喝一口水，都必須完全倚靠祂。以利亞會在旅程的每一步，都經歷神的手。

有時，神以極大的方式供應我們，彷彿突破突然臨到，一切都改變了。另一些時候，祂只在當下賜下我們正需要的，好讓我們學習知足，並記得信靠祂。不論是哪一種情況，你會怎樣信靠祂？

question.en: Think of a time when God gave you what you needed and not what you wanted. How did you grow through that time?
question.zh-Hant: 回想一次神賜給你所需、而不是你想要之物的經歷。你在那段時間裡如何成長？

question.en: How can you shift your perspective to see everything you have as a gift from God?
question.zh-Hant: 你可以怎樣調整眼光，把自己擁有的一切都看作神的恩賜？

prayer.en: Lord, help me to know the difference between my wants and my needs. Teach me to be thankful and content with what you give me. Help me to trust you.
prayer.zh-Hant: 主啊，求祢幫助我分辨自己的想要與需要。求祢教導我，為祢所賜的一切感恩和知足。求祢幫助我信靠祢。

content.en:
Most of us know what it feels like to really want something; many of us also know what it feels like to have more than enough. Do we know how it feels to be content, though? Contentment is satisfaction with what you have, not desiring more or less.

One of the greatest examples of contentment in the Bible comes from the apostle Paul. Before Paul met Jesus, he had quite the resume. Not only was he extremely smart, but he was also in charge of a lot of people and heavily mistreated Christians. Then one day, his life changed forever for the good! Jesus appeared to him in a miraculous way, and Paul surrendered his life to Him. Paul then went on a life-long journey to spread the gospel across the known world at that time. Paul had a radically different view of life, so much so, that he described his past accomplishments as if they didn’t matter anymore. You can read about this in Philippians 3. Everything about Paul changed because that’s what Jesus does: He transforms us and makes us new!

Paul wrote this letter to the church at Philippi from prison. He had experienced the highest of highs in life. Remember that resume? Paul had reached the height of his career and leadership, from a worldly sense, but from a prison cell, none of his worldly accomplishments mattered. Christ was enough! As a student, a lot of worldly desires try to steal your contentment, whether on a screen, in a relationship, with your grades, or in your athletic goals. You’ll struggle to be content when you’re constantly comparing what you have or don’t have to others. When your satisfaction is in Christ, then you can be content when those other things aren’t going well. When you build your life on Christ, then and only then, will you be content.
content.zh-Hant:
我們大多數人都知道非常想要某樣東西是甚麼感覺；許多人也知道擁有得綽綽有餘是甚麼感覺。然而，我們知道知足是甚麼感覺嗎？知足，就是滿足於自己所擁有的，不渴望更多，也不渴望更少。

聖經中最偉大的知足榜樣之一，就是使徒保羅。保羅遇見耶穌以前，履歷相當亮眼。他不但才智過人，也管轄許多人，還大力迫害基督徒。然而有一天，他的生命從此永遠變得更美好！耶穌以神蹟奇妙地向他顯現，保羅便把生命降服於祂。之後，保羅展開了一生的旅程，把福音傳遍當時人們所知道的世界。保羅對人生的看法徹底改變，甚至把過去的成就看作再也無關緊要。你可以在腓立比書第3章讀到這件事。保羅的一切都改變了，因為耶穌所做的正是這樣：祂改變我們，使我們成為新造的人！

保羅在監獄裡寫了這封信給腓立比教會。他曾經歷過人生最輝煌的高峰。還記得那份履歷嗎？從屬世的角度來看，保羅的事業和領導地位都已達到頂峰；但身在牢房裡，屬世的一切成就都不再重要。基督已經足夠！身為學生，許多屬世的慾望都想奪走你的知足，無論是螢幕上的東西、人際關係、成績，還是運動目標。當你不斷把自己擁有或缺少的，拿來和別人比較時，就很難知足。當你的滿足在基督裡，即使其他事情並不順利，你仍可以知足。唯有當你把生命建造在基督之上，你才能知足。

question.en: In what ways do you compare your life to others? How has this made being content more difficult?
question.zh-Hant: 你會在哪些方面把自己的生活與別人比較？這如何使知足變得更加困難？

question.en: What is at least one practical step you can take to live a life of more contentment? Write it down and try it!
question.zh-Hant: 你至少可以採取哪一個實際步驟，活出更知足的生命？把它寫下來，並付諸行動！

prayer.en: Lord, teach me to be content. This does not come easy or naturally for me. Open my eyes to all that you have given me and show me the better way of living that comes through a relationship with you!
prayer.zh-Hant: 主啊，求祢教導我知足。這對我來說並不容易，也不是出於本性。求祢開我的眼睛，看見祢所賜的一切，並讓我看見，藉著與祢相交而來那更美好的生活方式！

content.en:
Behind every gift is a giver. What’s your favorite gift you received at Christmas or on your birthday? You may have asked for this gift and had a feeling that you might get it, or maybe you were completely surprised. When you opened the gift, you were locked in on that moment. Full of excitement and anticipation, you were ready to enjoy that gift. Hopefully before you used the gift, you recognized and thanked the person who gave it to you. If it wasn’t for that person, the gift wouldn’t be yours, right?

Throughout Scripture, we read about God giving good gifts to His people, sometimes in unexpected ways. In Exodus, we see God’s wondrous work through Moses, as he embarked on the journey to free Israel from Egyptian slavery. God’s provision for His people came in many ways, but one way was through bringing plagues on the Egyptians. The Nile River was crucial to Egyptian survival and to their way of life. Pharaoh had previously thrown Hebrew male infants into the Nile as a method of cruel control (Ex. 1:22). But through Moses’s obedience, God changed the Nile River to blood as judgment on Egypt for mistreating His people. This act of provision for Israel’s release from slavery points to the ultimate provision of Jesus releasing us from slavery to sin. Many years later, Jesus transformed water again, this time into crimson wine—blessing instead of judgment. Do you see the connection? Jesus reversed the curse of judgment through His own blood, and this miracle at the wedding in Cana hinted at His perfect sacrifice. The water turned to wine foreshadowed that Jesus would provide for our deepest need—forgiveness for sin and freedom from judgment!
content.zh-Hant:
每一份禮物背後，都有一位送禮物的人。你在聖誕節或生日收到過的禮物中，最喜歡哪一份？你可能曾開口要這份禮物，也隱約覺得自己會收到；又或許，你完全沒有料到。打開禮物時，你全心投入那一刻。你滿懷興奮與期待，準備好好享受那份禮物。希望你在使用禮物以前，也有留意並感謝那位送禮物給你的人。若不是因為那個人，這份禮物就不會屬於你，對嗎？

整本聖經都記載神把美好的恩賜賜給祂的百姓，有時更以出人意料的方式賜下。在出埃及記裡，我們看見神藉摩西施行奇妙的作為；摩西踏上旅程，要使以色列人脫離埃及的奴役。神以許多方式供應祂的百姓，其中一種就是降災給埃及人。尼羅河對埃及人的生存和生活方式至關重要。先前，法老曾把希伯來男嬰丟進尼羅河，作為殘酷統治的手段（出埃及記 1:22）。但藉著摩西的順服，神把尼羅河變成血，審判埃及人虐待祂百姓的罪。神為使以色列人脫離奴役所作的供應，指向耶穌所成就的終極供應——使我們脫離罪的奴役。多年以後，耶穌再次使水改變，這次變成深紅色的酒——帶來祝福，而不是審判。你看見兩者之間的聯繫嗎？耶穌藉自己的血逆轉了審判的咒詛，而迦拿婚宴的這個神蹟，預示了祂完全的獻祭。水變為酒，預表耶穌會供應我們最深切的需要——罪得赦免，並脫離審判！

question.en: How often do you thank God for the amazing gift of freedom from sin and judgment?
question.zh-Hant: 你有多常為脫離罪和審判這份奇妙的恩賜感謝神？

question.en: Why do we often forget that our greatest gift is a relationship with Jesus? Why do we allow following Jesus to feel like a burden?
question.zh-Hant: 為甚麼我們常常忘記，自己最寶貴的恩賜就是與耶穌建立關係？為甚麼我們容許自己覺得跟從耶穌是一種負擔？

prayer.en: Lord, forgive me when I forget that every good gift comes from you. Thank you for loving me and for giving your son, Jesus. Give me the eyes to see your work in all things!
prayer.zh-Hant: 主啊，當我忘記一切美好的恩賜都從祢而來時，求祢赦免我。感謝祢愛我，又賜下祢的兒子耶穌。求祢賜我眼睛，在萬事中看見祢的工作！
